en.name: Canadian bacon, whole piece
en.summary: A whole piece of Canadian bacon keeps 2 weeks in the refrigerator at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and 2 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). Left whole it keeps far longer than the sliced version, because there is much less cut surface exposed.
en.pantry: It does not belong at room temperature at any stage. Canadian bacon is cured but it is not dry-cured to shelf stability — it is a moist, cooked, ready-to-eat meat, and the cure slows spoilage rather than preventing it. Bring it home cold and keep it cold. Out of the fridge it gets two hours at most, one hour if the room is above 32 °C (90 °F), and a piece that has been sitting out while you cook the rest of breakfast should go back in between uses.
en.fridge: 2 weeks at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, wrapped airtight in the coldest part of the fridge. Slicing is what shortens it: every cut face is new surface for bacteria, so cut off what you need and keep the rest of the piece whole and wrapped rather than slicing the lot in advance. Because this is eaten without further cooking, Listeria is the organism that matters — it grows slowly even in a cold fridge — and pregnant, elderly and immunocompromised people are generally advised to heat ready-to-eat cured meats until steaming hot.
en.freezer: 2 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Wrap it tightly in cling film and then foil or a freezer bag, pressing out the air; a whole piece is dense and dries out badly at the surface if air can reach it. The meat stays safe indefinitely at −18 °C, and the 2 months is a quality figure — beyond it the cure tastes harsher and the texture goes watery. If you are going to use it in pieces, cut it into meal-sized chunks before freezing rather than thawing and refreezing the whole thing.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge — allow a day for a substantial piece — or in cold water in a sealed bag with the water changed every half hour. Never thaw it on the counter, and do not refreeze it once thawed.
spoilage: A slimy or tacky surface film.
A sour, sulphurous or ammonia-like smell.
Grey, green or iridescent patches on a cut face.
A puffed or leaking vacuum pack.
tips: Keep the piece whole and slice to order; cut faces are what spoil first.
Wrap in cling film then foil before freezing to keep air off.
Cut into meal-sized pieces before freezing so you never refreeze.
Store on a cold shelf, not in the fridge door.

faq.q: How long does a whole piece of Canadian bacon keep?
faq.a: 2 weeks in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 2 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F).

faq.q: Why does a whole piece keep longer than slices?
faq.a: Slicing creates a great deal of new surface for bacteria and for drying. Keep the piece whole and cut only what you need.

faq.q: Does Canadian bacon need to be cooked?
faq.a: It is sold fully cooked. Pregnant, elderly and immunocompromised people are advised to heat ready-to-eat cured meats until steaming hot before eating.

zh.name: 加拿大培根（整塊）
zh.summary: 整塊的加拿大培根冷藏 4 °C 以下可放 2 週，冷凍 −18 °C 下 2 個月。維持整塊比切片耐放得多，因為暴露的切面少很多。
zh.pantry: 它在任何階段都不屬於室溫。加拿大培根有醃製，但並不是乾醃到可以常溫保存的程度——它是含水、已煮熟的即食肉品，醃製只是拖慢腐敗而不是阻止腐敗。買回來要保冷，回家後也要保冷。離開冰箱最多兩小時，室溫超過 32 °C 時最多一小時；煮其他早餐時放在旁邊的那一塊，中間應該先冰回去。
zh.fridge: 4 °C 以下 2 週，密封包好放冰箱最冷的位置。讓它變短的是切片：每一個切面都是細菌的新領地，所以要用多少切多少，其餘維持整塊並包好，不要事先全部切完。因為它不會再加熱就被吃掉，真正要提防的是李斯特菌——它在冷藏溫度下仍會緩慢生長。懷孕、年長與免疫功能低下者，一般建議把即食醃肉加熱到冒蒸氣再吃。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 2 個月。先用保鮮膜緊緊包住，再包鋁箔或裝進冷凍袋並把空氣壓掉；整塊肉密度高，一旦接觸空氣，表面會嚴重乾化。在 −18 °C 下它在安全上可以無限期保存，2 個月談的是品質——超過之後醃味會變得粗糙、質地也會出水。如果打算分次使用，請在冷凍前就切成一餐的份量，而不是整塊解凍後又冰回去。
zh.thawing: 放冷藏解凍——大塊請預留一天——或連密封袋泡冷水，每半小時換水。不要放室溫退冰，解凍後也不要再次冷凍。
spoilage: 表面出現黏滑或發黏的薄膜。
聞起來有酸味、硫味或氨味。
切面出現灰色、綠色或虹彩光澤的斑。
tips: 維持整塊、要吃再切，切面最先壞。
冷凍前先包保鮮膜再包鋁箔，隔絕空氣。
冷凍前先分成一餐份，就不會需要二次冷凍。
放冷藏層架，不要放冰箱門邊。

faq.q: 整塊加拿大培根可以放多久？
faq.a: 冷藏 4 °C 以下 2 週，或冷凍 −18 °C 下 2 個月。

faq.q: 為什麼整塊比切片耐放？
faq.a: 切片會製造大量新的表面，既讓細菌有機可乘也容易乾掉。請維持整塊，要用多少切多少。
它販售時已經完全煮熟。但懷孕、年長與免疫功能低下者，建議把即食醃肉加熱到冒蒸氣再吃。
